requirements_summary.summary: Participium is a web application for the Municipality of Turin enabling citizens to report urban issues (e.g., potholes, lighting) via an interactive map and form. Reports undergo a lifecycle: Pending Approval -> Assigned -> In Progress -> Resolved/Rejected/Suspended. Citizens can register with email confirmation, choose anonymity, and receive notifications via platform or Telegram bot. Technical offices manage reports, assign external maintainers (with or without system access), and update statuses. System administrators configure users, roles, and automatic assignment rules.

requirements.text:
As a technical office staff member
I want to assign reports to external maintainers
So that specialized maintainers can handle and update the intervention.
constraints: It can be possible for specific reports of certain categories (e.g., Enel X for category Public Lighting) based on their content reviewed by the technical office staff member.
expected_behaviors: specialized maintainers can handle and update the intervention

requirements.text:
As an external maintainer 
I want to update the status of a report assigned to me
So that I can updated citizens about  the intervention.
expected_behaviors: I can updated citizens about  the intervention

requirements.text:
As a citizen
I want to register with my name and username 
So that I can access the Participium system and submit reports.
constraints: Registration is required before submitting reports.
expected_behaviors: I can access the Participium system and submit reports

requirements.text:
As a system administrator
I want to set up municipality users
constraints: These are the internal accounts of the municipality

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to select a location on the city map
So that my report is geolocated with latitude and longitude.
constraints: Reports must be tied to a specific location. Use OpenStreet Map (or any other derivative map based on it), standard layer
expected_behaviors: my report is geolocated with latitude and longitude

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to provide details for my report 
So that the the problem is classified correctly.
constraints: Mandatory fields: title, description,  category , photos (min 1 max 3).
expected_behaviors: the the problem is classified correctly

requirements.text:
As a municipal public relations officer
I want to review and approve or reject reports 
So that only valid reports are processed further.
constraints: Rejected reports must include an explanation. If accepted, the report is assigned to the technical office bound to the report category.
expected_behaviors: only valid reports are processed further

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to choose whether to make my report anonymous 
So that my name is not shown in the public list of reports.
constraints: Anonymous option protects privacy. Choice made at issue description time.
expected_behaviors: my name is not shown in the public list of reports

requirements.text:
As a technical office staff member
I want to see the list of reports assigned to me
So that I can get an overview of the maintenance to be done
expected_behaviors: I can get an overview of the maintenance to be done

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to configure my account
So that I can better manage notifications and my virtual presence.
constraints: Citizens can  upload a personal photo, add their Telegram username and switch off/on email notifications in the configuration panel.
expected_behaviors: I can better manage notifications and my virtual presence

requirements.text:
As a technical office staff member 
I want to update report statuses 
So that citizens are informed of the problem resolution process.
constraints: At each status change, the citizen receives notification in the platform with the corresponding update. Municipal operators working on reports can also send messages to the citizens in the platform, to which the citizen can reply.
expected_behaviors: citizens are informed of the problem resolution process

requirements.text:
As a citizen/unregistered user
I want to browse a summary table of reports with filters 
So that I can easily explore and analyze existing reports.
constraints: Filters: by category, status, period of time
expected_behaviors: I can easily explore and analyze existing reports

domain_rules: Reports must be tied to a specific location using OpenStreetMap (standard layer).

Report categories include: Water Supply, Architectural Barriers, Sewer System, Public Lighting, Waste, Road Signs and Traffic Lights, Roads and Urban Furnishings, Public Green Areas and Playgrounds, Other.
Report statuses are: Pending Approval, Assigned, In Progress, Suspended, Rejected, Resolved.
Once a report is inserted, it cannot be modified or deleted by the citizen.
Anonymous user's name is visible to staff but hidden in the public map view for citizens.
Only technical office staff members can have multiple roles.
External maintainers are added by the system administrator and must have their own individual account.
Case 1 (External maintainer has access): Comments/information exchanged between technical office and external maintainer are report-specific and reserved (not visible to reporter/citizens).
Case 2 (External maintainer no access): Communication is out of scope; technical office updates status externally and moves report to 'Resolved'.
Public statistics include number of reports by category and trends by day/week/month.
Private statistics (admin only) include detailed breakdowns by status, type, reporter, and combinations including top 1% and 5% reporters.
Email is a mandatory field for registration and can be used for login.
Municipal public relations officer and municipal administrator roles are automatically associated with the Organization Office.
Public Relation officer can assign a report to a specific technical office or directly to a staff member of that office.
Specific technical offices must be set up in project documentation with defined report categories.
edge_cases: User attempts to submit a report without registering: System blocks submission until registration and confirmation are complete.
Confirmation code expires (30 minutes): User cannot activate account until new code is requested or valid code entered.
Citizen chooses anonymity: Name hidden in public views but visible to staff for internal tracking.
Report rejected: Explanation from Municipality Organization Office is mandatory and must be displayed.
External maintainer resolves report (Case 1): Status moves to 'Resolved' without technical office intervention if work is finished.
External maintainer cannot resolve report (Case 2): Technical office staff member must manually move status to 'Resolved'.
Zooming out on map: Reports grouped into cumulative view showing total count.
Filtering table view: Downloaded CSV contains only filtered data if a filter is active.
Following closed reports: System prevents following; only open reports can be followed.
Telegram bot commands for non-existent report ID: System should handle gracefully (e.g., show error or list available options).
Email notifications disabled in config: User receives only platform notifications, no emails.
assumptions: The 'Organization Office' refers to the central administrative body responsible for initial review and assignment logic.
Competent technical office is determined by the problem category (e.g., Public Lighting -> Enel X or specific office).
Telegram bot integration requires users to provide a valid Telegram username in their profile configuration.
Push notifications via Telegram are real-time unless explicitly unsubscribed.
The map layer used is strictly OpenStreetMap standard layer as per design constraints.
Automatic assignment logic applies globally to all issues of a certain category if enabled by admin.
External maintainers added by system administrator implies a specific workflow for onboarding external companies.
Statistics calculations (e.g., top 1%) are based on the number of reports submitted per reporter.
